newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Troop reinforcements have poured into Tak province after pro-Rangoon renegades threatened to attack Tha Song Yang town and Mae La refugee camp. The Democratic Karen Buddhist Army threat has forced 1,000 Thais to flee three border villages and 20,000 Karen civilians in Mae La to evacuate deeper into the hinterland along the Mae Sot-Mae Sariang road. (BANGKOK POST)

- A narcotics syndicate plans to assassinate the prime minister and two other ministers, says Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung. Though he did not name the other ministers, they were later identified as Sanoh Thienthong, his boss, and himself. The government's relentless crackdowns on drugs have incurred the wrath of what he called a vicious ring. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Singapore is unhappy with Deputy Prime Minister Montree Pongpanit's claim that a nearby country bribed senior Thai ministers in an attempt to kill plans for Bangkok's second international airport, says Deputy Prime Minister Korn Dabaransi. Montree mentioned neither the country's name nor the Cabinet members allegedly involved. His claim came after a member of his party was accused of signing a contract to buy overpriced sand to fill the proposed airport site. (THE NATION)

- Charoen Pokphand Group sees multimedia programming and the production of integrated circuits as businesses of great interest to the group. The company chairman says he is impressed with the success of U.S.-based business group Viacom which found success through the production of children's programming and music videos. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Prime Minister's Office is expected to call for bids on a new ultra high frequency television (UHF) licence later this year, with plans to modify Independent Television's terms of reference for the new licence. The licence will lead to the establishment of Thailand's seventh free-to-air television station, in addition to more than 40 channels on three subscription television networks. (THE NATION)

- Alphatec Group, which is building two computer chip wafer fabrication plants on the eastern seaboard from which it plans to export 75 to 100 billion baht worth of electronics annually from 1998, has established a foothold in the Asia-Pacific market by opening a subsidiary in Tokyo, called Alphatec Japan Co Ltd. (THE NATION)
